observations.text: SP completed the gyro-out GCA to the level desired for this stage, with the IP directing the no-gyro turns and part of the final descent. Altitude until on final was allowed to reach 300 feet before the IP's direction, and the standby compass turns were started only when prompted. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent initiation of the timed no-gyro turns is expected to improve.

SP flew the gyro-out GCA with the IP's verbal prompts only, holding altitude until on final within 300 feet and rolling out within 10 degrees of the headings assigned by the final controller. Airspeed on final was kept inside the +20/-10 knot band, and the deviations were recognized and corrected with delay but without IP intervention on the controls. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the gyro-out GCA without IP intervention, using timed standard-rate turns and the needle, ball and airspeed presentation to comply with the controller's no-gyro instructions. Small errors of up to 200 feet in altitude until on final and up to 8 degrees in heading were recognized and self-corrected in a timely manner. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the gyro-out GCA accurately and promptly, complying with every no-gyro turn instruction without IP intervention. Altitude until on final was held within 100 feet, heading within 4 degrees of the assigned values and airspeed within +8/-4 knots, while the glide path was regained after only slight excursions above it. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the gyro-out GCA with exceptional precision, anticipating each controller instruction and rolling out on the assigned heading without overshoot. Deviations in altitude until on final, heading and airspeed were negligible, and the aircraft arrived at the decision point on centerline and on the glide path. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to retention of a scan pattern built around the attitude indicator, did not transition to the partial-panel presentation of needle, ball and airspeed after the gyro failure. The turns to the controller's assigned headings were flown untimed and altitude until on final departed by more than 400 feet, with the result that the IP had to direct the turns and execute part of the descent. Further practice of the no-gyro instrument cross-check is required.

SP, due to insufficient recent practice in raw-data manual flying, could not complete the gyro-out GCA without assistance. Heading departed more than 15 degrees from the values assigned by the final controller and airspeed on final reached 25 knots above the target, with the result that the IP directed the heading corrections and executed part of the final segment. Partial-panel work before the next instrument sortie is required.

SP completed the gyro-out GCA within the standards for this stage, but the controller's no-gyro turn instructions were followed only after the IP's verbal prompts. Altitude until on final reached 300 feet on two occasions and heading settled 10 degrees from the assigned value before correction. Marginal performance for the Training Section - timely recognition of the standby compass turn rate is expected to improve.

SP flew the gyro-out GCA without IP intervention, timing the no-gyro turns and complying with the final controller's instructions from the standby compass. Minor errors of up to 200 feet in altitude until on final and up to 15 knots above the target airspeed were recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the gyro-out GCA accurately and promptly, complying with each no-gyro instruction without prompting. Altitude until on final was held within 120 feet, heading within 4 degrees of the assigned values and airspeed within +8/-4 knots, and altitude at MDA was held 60 feet high with no descent below the published figure. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the gyro-out GCA with exceptional precision, cross-checking timed standard-rate turns against the standby compass so that every no-gyro instruction was met on the first roll-out. Deviations in altitude until on final, heading and airspeed were negligible, and the aircraft remained on the glide path from the final descent point to the decision point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a turn technique based on bank angle rather than on timed standard rate after the gyro failure, did not comply with the controller's no-gyro turn instructions. Roll-out was short of the assigned heading by more than 15 degrees on the standby compass and altitude until on final exceeded 400 feet, with the result that the IP directed each subsequent turn. The approach was not completed without assistance.

SP, due to workload distribution that left the SP flying, navigating and transmitting at the same time, did not maintain the partial-panel cross-check during the gyro-out GCA. Airspeed on final decreased 15 knots below the target and the aircraft was allowed to descend more than 200 feet below the glide path, with the result that the IP intervened on the controls to arrest the descent. The approach was discontinued and re-flown under IP direction.

SP, due to an unstabilized power setting at the final descent point, did not hold the airspeed and descent rate called for by the gyro-out GCA profile. Airspeed on final reached 20 knots above the target and altitude until on final reached 300 feet, and both were corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. Recognition and correction were delayed.

SP, due to attention captured by a minor system indication while the aircraft state went unmonitored, did not follow the final controller's no-gyro heading corrections on the intermediate segment. Heading reached 10 degrees from the assigned value and altitude until on final reached 300 feet, both corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. Errors were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP flew the gyro-out GCA within the desired standards and corrected the deviations without IP intervention; however, two heading excursions of 8 degrees on the standby compass and one excursion of 200 feet in altitude until on final had to be re-corrected. Marginal performance for the Training Section - anticipation of the lead point for the standby compass roll-out is expected to improve.

SP executed the gyro-out GCA accurately and promptly, complying with each controller instruction without IP intervention. Altitude until on final was held within 100 feet, heading within 5 degrees and airspeed within +10/-5 knots, and altitude at MDA was maintained 50 feet high with no descent below the published value. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the gyro-out GCA with exceptional precision, flying timed standard-rate turns cross-checked against the standby compass so that each no-gyro instruction was met without overshoot. Altitude, heading and airspeed deviations were negligible throughout the approach and the aircraft reached the decision point on centerline and on profile. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to omission of the gyro-out procedure and of the identification of the failed instruments before commencing the approach, did not set up the partial-panel presentation required for the no-gyro GCA. Turns to the assigned headings were flown beyond standard rate with heading errors above 15 degrees, while altitude until on final departed by more than 400 feet. The IP had to direct the approach and execute part of the final descent.

SP, due to a false attitude perception that was not resolved against the instruments during the no-gyro turn, did not maintain wings level or the descent profile on final. Airspeed increased 30 knots above the target and the aircraft descended more than 250 feet below the glide path, with the result that the IP took the controls and executed the go-around. Recovery from the undesired aircraft state was not initiated by the SP.

SP, due to failure to allow for standby compass lag during the turns, did not roll out on the headings assigned by the final controller. Heading errors reached 10 degrees and altitude until on final reached 300 feet, corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. Recognition and correction were delayed throughout the intermediate segment.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, did not complete the landing configuration in time to stabilize the gyro-out GCA. Airspeed on final reached 20 knots above the target and the aircraft was allowed to reach 300 feet above the glide path, both corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. The errors were recognized late and the SP remained behind the aircraft until the decision point.

SP, due to a late power reduction at the final descent point, did not establish the descent rate called for by the gyro-out GCA profile. Airspeed on final reached 15 knots above the target and altitude until on final reached 200 feet, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. The remainder of the approach was flown within the desired parameters.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established on final, did not maintain the continuous heading corrections called for by the no-gyro controller. Heading reached 8 degrees from the assigned value and the aircraft drifted 200 feet high in altitude until on final, with both deviations recognized and self-corrected without IP intervention. Small errors only, corrected in a timely manner.

SP executed the gyro-out GCA without IP intervention, holding altitude until on final within 140 feet, heading within 5 degrees of the assigned values and airspeed within +10/-5 knots. However, the corrections at the final descent point were applied at the edge of the desired band and the glide path was regained slightly late on two occasions. Marginal performance for the Training Section - smoother anticipation of the no-gyro turn instructions is expected to improve.

SP executed the gyro-out GCA with exceptional precision, anticipating each no-gyro instruction and holding the timed standard-rate turns without overshoot. Deviations in altitude until on final, heading, airspeed and glide path were negligible, and the descent to MDA was flown with no excursion below the published altitude. Above end of block MIF achieved.
